# Evaluation Plan

## Problem Grounding

### 1. Who specifically has the collaboration problem?

University students working in small teams on semester-long software or programming projects.

### 2. What do they currently do instead of our tool?

They currently use tools such as Discord, LINE, Google Docs, GitHub, and verbal discussion to coordinate tasks, share updates, and track responsibilities. Important information can become scattered across different platforms.

### 3. What would be observably different if our tool worked?

Team members would be able to quickly identify who is responsible for each task, check the current task status, and find unresolved issues without searching through multiple messages or documents.

## Evaluation Plan

### Success Definition

We will know our tool works if users can identify task ownership, task status, and unresolved work more quickly and accurately than with their current workflow.

If AI is used, the AI will suggest relevant tasks, summaries, or issues that may require attention. Human users will make the final decision about whether the suggestion is correct and what action should be taken.

### Target Users

Our target users are university students who have experience working on group programming or software projects.

We plan to recruit participants from classmates or other students who have previously worked on team-based projects.

### Method

We will use structured observation followed by a brief interview.

Participants will be asked to complete several collaboration-related tasks using our tool, such as finding the owner of a task or identifying unresolved work. We will observe whether they can complete the tasks successfully and how long it takes.

Afterward, we will ask short interview questions about usability, usefulness, and whether the tool improved their collaboration workflow.

### Minimum Evidence Threshold

We will test with at least five participants.

We will consider the initial evaluation promising if at least four out of five participants can complete the main tasks successfully and most participants report that the tool makes collaboration information easier to find or understand.
